# Rules

<!-- Generated by PROSA_RULES_CATALOG=1 go test ./rules/ -run TestCatalogUpToDate. Do not edit. -->

A rule is a best practice written in prose. The planner reads the rules that apply to the resource types of a plan, and a reviewer checks the plan against them before you see it.

- Disable a rule for the project: list its ID in `rules/disabled.txt`, or pass `--disable-rule ID` for one run.
- Make an exception: name the rule ID in the prose of the intent, with the reason.
- Add your own: write a Markdown file under `rules/` with the same front matter (`id`, `title`, `applies_to`, `source`) and the rule as prose. Give it your own ID prefix (e.g. `ACME-NET-001`), never the provider's (`AWS-`), so that a future Prosa release cannot collide with it.

## AWS

### AWS-DATA-001 — Databases keep automatic backups

Applies to: `aws_db_instance`, `aws_rds_cluster`

`backup_retention_period` is greater than 0; 7 days is the recommended value.
A replica may inherit its source's backups.

Source:
- [AWS Security Hub, RDS.11](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/securityhub/latest/userguide/rds-controls.html)

### AWS-ENC-001 — Database storage is encrypted at rest

Applies to: `aws_db_instance`, `aws_rds_cluster`

`storage_encrypted` is `true`. When a key is named (`kms_key_id`), it is a
customer managed key only if the intent asks for one; otherwise the AWS
managed key is enough.

Source:
- [AWS Security Hub, RDS.3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/securityhub/latest/userguide/rds-controls.html)

### AWS-ENC-002 — HTTPS listeners use a current TLS policy

Applies to: `aws_lb_listener`

A listener with `protocol` HTTPS or TLS sets `ssl_policy` to a TLS 1.2 or
1.3 policy such as `ELBSecurityPolicy-TLS13-1-2-Res-2021-06`, never an older
one such as `ELBSecurityPolicy-2016-08`. When an Application Load Balancer has
an HTTPS listener, its port 80 listener redirects to HTTPS instead of
forwarding. A load balancer with no HTTPS listener is not a violation of this
rule.

Source:
- [AWS Security Hub, ELB.17](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/securityhub/latest/userguide/elb-controls.html#elb-17)
- [AWS Security Hub, ELB.1](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/securityhub/latest/userguide/elb-controls.html#elb-1)

### AWS-IAM-001 — Policies grant only the actions and resources needed

Applies to: `aws_iam_policy`, `aws_iam_role_policy`

Every `Allow` statement in `policy` lists the specific actions the workload
uses and the ARNs of the resources it touches. No statement has `"Action": "*"`
with `"Resource": "*"`, and a `*` in either is justified only where the API
accepts no resource-level scoping.

Source:
- [AWS Well-Architected, SEC03-BP02](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/latest/security-pillar/sec_permissions_least_privileges.html)
- [AWS Security Hub, IAM.1](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/securityhub/latest/userguide/iam-controls.html#iam-1)

### AWS-IAM-002 — ECS tasks have separate execution and task roles

Applies to: `aws_ecs_task_definition`, `aws_iam_role`

A task definition sets `execution_role_arn` to a role that pulls images,
writes logs, and reads only the secrets and parameters its container
definitions reference with `valueFrom`, and `task_role_arn` to a different
role holding the application's own permissions. Everything the application
itself calls goes on the task role, never on the execution role.

Source:
- [Amazon ECS, task execution IAM role](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/task_execution_IAM_role.html)
- [Amazon ECS, task IAM role](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/task-iam-roles.html)

### AWS-LOG-001 — Container logs go to CloudWatch with a retention

Applies to: `aws_ecs_task_definition`, `aws_cloudwatch_log_group`

Each container in `container_definitions` has a `logConfiguration` with the
`awslogs` driver and a log group created by the plan. That
`aws_cloudwatch_log_group` sets `retention_in_days` explicitly; never leave
it unset, which keeps logs forever.

Source:
- [AWS Security Hub, ECS.9](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/securityhub/latest/userguide/ecs-controls.html#ecs-9)
- [AWS Security Hub, CloudWatch.16](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/securityhub/latest/userguide/cloudwatch-controls.html)

### AWS-NET-001 — A database accepts traffic only from its clients

Applies to: `aws_security_group`, `aws_vpc_security_group_ingress_rule`, `aws_db_instance`

The database's security group allows its port only from the security groups
of the workloads that use it, referenced by their id. Never from a CIDR: not
0.0.0.0/0, not the VPC, not a subnet.

Source:
- [AWS Well-Architected, SEC05-BP02](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/latest/security-pillar/sec_network_protection_layered.html)

### AWS-NET-002 — Ingress from the whole internet only on 80 and 443 of a public load balancer

Applies to: `aws_security_group`, `aws_vpc_security_group_ingress_rule`, `aws_security_group_rule`

No ingress rule has a source of 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0 (`cidr_ipv4`, `cidr_ipv6`,
`cidr_blocks`, `ipv6_cidr_blocks`), with one exception: TCP 80 and 443 on the
security group of a public load balancer. Any other port, and any other
resource, is reached from a security group or from a narrower CIDR.

Source:
- [AWS Security Hub, EC2.18 and EC2.19](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/securityhub/latest/userguide/ec2-controls.html)
- [AWS Well-Architected, SEC05-BP01](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/latest/security-pillar/sec_network_protection_create_layers.html)

### AWS-NET-003 — Databases are not publicly accessible

Applies to: `aws_db_instance`, `aws_rds_cluster_instance`

`publicly_accessible` is `false` (or left unset, as its default is false), and
the database sits in a DB subnet group made of private subnets.

Source:
- [AWS Security Hub, RDS.2](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/securityhub/latest/userguide/rds-controls.html)

### AWS-NET-004 — ECS tasks behind a load balancer have no public IP

Applies to: `aws_ecs_service`

A service with a `load_balancer` block sets `assign_public_ip` to `false` in
`network_configuration` and runs in private subnets; the load balancer is the
only public entry point. A task that must reach the internet does so through
a NAT gateway or VPC endpoints.

Source:
- [AWS Security Hub, ECS.2](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/securityhub/latest/userguide/ecs-controls.html#ecs-2)
- [AWS Well-Architected, SEC05-BP01](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/latest/security-pillar/sec_network_protection_create_layers.html)
